subject: Logic
title: The Limits of Fallacy Labels
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Limits of Fallacy Labels usable.

hook.text: "That's a strawman!" shouted in every online debate. But naming a fallacy isn't the same as refuting one.

buildup.text: Fallacy labels are tools for analysis, not weapons for argument. Dropping names doesn't prove you right.

discovery.text: Sometimes what looks like a fallacy isn't one in context. Appeals to experts within their field are valid.

twist.text: Over-labeling fallacies can itself become a fallacy—dismissing arguments without engaging their substance.

climax.text: Use fallacy knowledge to understand reasoning, not to score points. Engage the argument first.

punchline.text: Name the flaw, then address it.

quiz.question: What's wrong with just naming a fallacy without further argument?
